name: Sathrah's Sacrifice
summary: At the Temple of the Moon, Sathrah's Sacrifice offers Lady Sathrah's spirit a chance at peace. Her silvery spinnerets come from the mighty spider who dwells in Teldrassil.

sections.title: Purification in the Holy Waters
sections.body: Lady Sathrah was a venerable creature of Teldrassil, until creeping madness and corruption spread through the great tree's boughs and took hold of her. The Sisterhood of Elune asks you to bring back her silvery spinnerets as a consecrated offering, not a trophy. At the fountain in the Temple of the Moon, the remains are bathed in holy water. The rite washes away the taint that poisoned Sathrah's mind and frees her troubled soul. Her spirit then appears peacefully within the sanctuary, with the promise of rebirth under Elune's grace.

faq.answer: Sathrah's Sacrifice is an offering of silvery spinnerets taken from Lady Sathrah, a mighty spider corrupted in Teldrassil. The Sisterhood of Elune uses them in a rite to cleanse her soul.

faq.q: Why must the spinnerets be placed in the fountain?
faq.answer: The fountain in Darnassus's Temple of the Moon holds holy water consecrated to Elune. Submerging Sathrah's remains washes away the corruption that drove her mad and releases her spirit from agony.

faq.q: What happens when the offering is presented?
faq.answer: When you place the offering in the sacred waters, the corruption is purged and Lady Sathrah's spectral form appears. She walks serenely around the pool, showing that her soul is at peace.
Priestess A'moora oversees the rite. A servant of the Sisterhood of Elune stationed in the Temple of the Moon, she directs you to lay Sathrah to rest and offer her remains to the goddess.

angles.text: As a night elf, you know that putting down corrupted wildlife is a somber duty. Returning Lady Sathrah's spirit to Elune's grace honors that duty.
As a priest, you can see the rite as an act of divine mercy. The Sisterhood of Elune uses holy waters to cleanse taint, rather than merely discarding the slain beast.
